text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — thanks for the feedback today. I sketched a minimal policy plugin shape we can iterate on, and a migration path that avoids a big bang. PTAL: https://redwood.example/r/rfc/policy-plugin-shape

kevin: looked good. question: do we want the plugin to return absolute costs or a normalized score? mixing both feels risky when we aggregate across regions.

maria: good call. proposal: plugin returns a typed list of candidates with both fields but we treat 'score' as primary for ranking and 'cost_estimate' as advisory. that keeps runtime cheap while letting ops tune cost-driven fallbacks.

siva: cache invalidation is the tricky bit. if plugins can return per-tenant overrides, we need TTL semantics. can we require a ``cache_ttl_seconds`` on each candidate? otherwise we end up with stale affinity.

maria: yes — require ``cache_ttl_seconds`` (0 allowed for no-cache). also have a flag ``is_sticky`` for affinity heuristics.

aj: from infra side, we need the API to be async-friendly. plugins should be able to stream partial scores back (best-effort) so the router can make a fast decision and then reconcile if a better candidate arrives. otherwise we'll bloat p99.

maria: agreed. rough API sketch: 
```json
{
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "edge-eu-1", "score": 0.82, "cost_estimate": 0.004, "cache_ttl_seconds": 60, "meta": {"region": "eu"}, "is_sticky": false}
  ],
  "diagnostics": "optional string for logs/breakdown",
  "partial": false
}
```

kevin: looks fine. want to call out that the runtime will normalize scores per-call context (latency-first vs cost-first). we should document normalization formula so plugin authors can reason about outputs.

maria: yes, I added a normalization appendix in the doc. short version: plugins should output raw utility numbers; router will convert using per-route weight vector (w_latency, w_cost, w_affinity) and a bounded transform so values stay in [-10,10].

carol: for rollout, +1 to a staged migration. suggested steps: 1) keep legacy resolver, 2) feature-flag policy-plugin path, 3) canary 5% traffic with live metrics, 4) open to 25/50 then full. add automated regression gates on p95 latency and unit-cost.

maria: that's the plan. one addition: add a compatibility adapter that maps legacy bucket weights into the new score shape so old policies keep working while we onboard. minimal compute overhead.

siva: adapter is smart — make it a compiled fast path in the router so we don't invoke JS plugins for every request.

aj: metrics/tracing: emit per-decision telemetry: chosen_candidate_id, score_components (latency_score, cost_score), decision_latency_ms, plugin_latency_ms. these feed the rollout gates.

maria: will add schema. also propose a small reference impl in go and py so infra + ML authors can test locally.

kevin: testing: add unit tests for normalization and an integration harness that can fuzz plugin outputs to ensure stability under adversarial scores.

maria: yep — test harness + perf benchmark (qps vs plugin-latency) on eng-runtime infra. target is <2ms median decision overhead for adapter path, <10ms for plugin path at 99th.

carol: minor ops ask: include a "fallback_policy" field per candidate: {"type": "fallback-to-stable", "priority": 10} so router can auto-fail to configured fallbacks without extra policy lookups. reduces double-lookup cost.

maria: good suggestion — adding fallback metadata.

rollout-bot: deploy request: canary feature-flag "policy-plugin-v1" scheduled for 1719018000 UTC — approvers: @carol @aj @siva

aj: acked for canary window, I'll add the gating dashboards and alerts.

kevin: I'll start a branch for the adapter + normalization tests. ping me when you have the swagger for the plugin endpoint.

maria: thanks all — I'll update the RFC with the API sketch, TTL and fallback bits, and the rollout plan. will tag owners and open the canary PR tomorrow.
